title_ar: محاضرة للشيخ الددو تنظمها جمعية المرأة للثقافة والتربية
title_en: A Lecture by Shaykh al-Dedew Organised by the Women's Association for Culture and Education
body_ar:
"المرأة بين ثقافات الشعوب وكرامة الوجود" كان عنوان محاضرة ألقاها فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو في مُدَرّج دار الشباب القديمة، وهي المحاضرة الأولى ضمن الأسبوع الثقافي التي تنظمه جمعية المرأة للتربية والثقافة، وقد حضر هذا النشاط نخبة من العلماء والمثقفين والساسة يمثلون أطيافا عدة، كما حضر جمهور نسوي غفير.

حاضر الشيخ عن الدور الرائد للمرأة في الدين والمجتمع والسياسة، وأبرز ريادتها في كل مجالات الحياة، وأن مناصفتها للأدوار مع الرجال تقتضيه حكمة التوازن في الكون، وتكلم عن جانب الحريات في المجتمع مستعرضا في ذلك التراث الفقهي والخصوصية الشنقيطية في الجانب الاجتماعي.

وأعطى أمثلة من الصحابيات الجليلات اللواتي جسدن أروع مثال في التضحية والبذل والعلم..، " فهن أكثر من روى السنن التطبيقية في الحديث.."، "ولم يَعرف تاريخ الأمة كله امرأة جرحت ولا تركت في علم الجرح والتعديل.. وهذا فضل عظيم" " فخديجة بنت خويلد ضربت أروع مثال في التضحية والمواساة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتثبيته على الحق؛ "إنك لتصل الرحم وتقري الضيف.."، وهي أول من آمن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الإطلاق، وكذلك كانت المرأة أول من ضحت بنفسها في سبيل الله؛ فالسيدة سمية بنت خياط –رضي الله عنها أول شهيدة في الإسلام كما كانت أول من هاجر في سبيل الله..، وتتعدد أسماء الصحابيات اللآتي اشتهرن بالعلم وكثرة الرواية، وتحفل كتب الحديث والرواية والطبقات بالنساء اللآتي رَوَيْن ورُوِيّ عنهن الحديث الشريف، مثل: أسماء بنت أبي بكر، وأسماء بنت عميس، وجويرية بنت الحارث، وحفصة بنت عمر، وزينب بنت جحش رضي الله عنهن، وتأتي أم المؤمنين عائشة رضي الله عنها في مقدمة رواة الحديث؛ فهي الفصيحة البليغة العالمة بالأنساب والأشعار، تروي بعض الآثار أن عندها نصف العلم، لذا كانت مقصد فقهاء الصحابة في بعض المسائل الفقهية المستعصية...

ونشير إلى أن وقت هذه المحاضرة كان وجيزا إذ توقفت الكلمة لأداء صلاة المغرب ولم يتسني للمنظمين إمكانية مواصلة أنشطتهم بعد الصلاة بسبب انقطاع التيار الكهربائي عن مكان التظاهرة، فاضطر الشيخ الددو إلى ختمها بالدعاء، دون مكبر للصوت، وأعلن عن انتهاء المحاضرة، وبدأ الجمهور الغفير رجالا ونساء بالانصراف.

للإستماع للمحاضرة الرجاء الضغط هنــا
body_en:
'Woman between the Cultures of Peoples and the Dignity of Existence' was the title of a lecture delivered by his eminence the erudite Shaykh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew in the lecture hall of the old Youth House. It was the first lecture of the cultural week organised by the Women's Association for Education and Culture. A select gathering of scholars, intellectuals and politicians representing several currents attended the event, as did a large audience of women.

The Shaykh lectured on the pioneering role of women in religion, society and politics, and brought out their leading part in every field of life, and that their sharing of roles equally with men is required by the wisdom of balance in the universe. He spoke about the aspect of liberties in society, surveying in this the juristic heritage and the particularity of the Shinqiti tradition on the social side.

He gave examples of the illustrious women Companions who embodied the finest example of sacrifice, giving and knowledge..: 'They are the greatest transmitters of the applied sunnah in hadith..'; 'The entire history of the community has not known a woman who was impugned, nor one who was left aside, in the science of appraising narrators.. and this is a great distinction.' 'Khadijah bint Khuwaylid set the finest example of sacrifice and of consoling the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and of making him firm upon the truth: "You keep the ties of kinship and you are hospitable to the guest.."' And she was the first of all to believe in the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Likewise a woman was the first to sacrifice herself in the path of God: the lady Sumayyah bint Khayyat, God be pleased with her, was the first martyr in Islam, just as she was the first to emigrate in the path of God.. And the names of the women Companions renowned for knowledge and for abundant transmission are many; the books of hadith and of transmission and of the generations are filled with women who transmitted and from whom the noble hadith was transmitted — such as Asma bint Abi Bakr, Asma bint ʿUmays, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, Hafsah bint ʿUmar and Zaynab bint Jahsh, God be pleased with them. And the Mother of the Believers ʿA'isha, God be pleased with her, comes foremost among the transmitters of hadith: she was eloquent and articulate, learned in genealogies and in poetry, and some reports relate that half of knowledge was with her, which is why she was the recourse of the jurists among the Companions in certain intractable questions of law...

We note that the time available for this lecture was brief, since the address was stopped for the performance of the sunset prayer, and it was not possible for the organisers to continue their activities after the prayer because of a power cut at the venue of the event. So Shaykh al-Dedew was obliged to close it with a supplication, without a loudspeaker, and announced the end of the lecture, and the large audience, men and women, began to disperse.

flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The title names the association 'for Culture and Education' and the body names it 'for Education and Culture' — the same two words in reversed order. One of the two is wrong and there is no way to tell which from the page. Both are preserved as the source has them, in Arabic and in English. The Sheikh's office should confirm the association's actual name before publication.

flags.arabic: حاضر الشيخ عن الدور الرائد للمرأة … وأن مناصفتها للأدوار مع الرجال تقتضيه حكمة التوازن في الكون
flags.context: the site's own summary of what the Sheikh said
options: render faithfully and mark that this is the site's report, not the Sheikh's words

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY, AND EDITORIALLY SIGNIFICANT. This record is a news report written by the site's editors, not a text by the Sheikh. Most of it paraphrases him in the third person, and only the passages in quotation marks purport to be his words. The distinction matters a great deal here, because the paraphrase attributes to him a substantial position on women's roles — including that women share roles equally with men as the wisdom of balance in the universe requires — which is reported, not quoted. The site must make unmistakably clear that this is a report about a lecture and not a text by the Sheikh, and the quoted and paraphrased material must be visually distinguished. Nothing has been added or removed in translation.

flags.arabic: ولم يَعرف تاريخ الأمة كله امرأة جرحت ولا تركت في علم الجرح والتعديل
flags.context: one of the passages given as the Sheikh's own words
options: a woman who was impugned, nor one who was left aside, in the science of appraising narrators
a woman who was declared unreliable or abandoned as a transmitter
a woman criticised or discarded in the appraisal of narrators
flags.note: The two verbs are technical terms of al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl: jaraḥa is to impugn a transmitter's reliability, and taraka is to abandon a transmitter as unusable. The claim is a strong and specific one about the hadith literature and is given as a direct quotation of the Sheikh. The English keeps the technical vocabulary rather than paraphrasing, so that the claim can be assessed for what it is.

translator_notes: Unlike the rest of this slice, the date on this record is most probably genuine: it is a news report of a specific event, and 25 December 2010 is consistent with its content. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set false here, against true everywhere else in the slice.
This is a site news item written by the editors in the third person, not a text by the Sheikh, and is typed news for that reason. It is the only news item in the slice.

The quotation marks, ellipses and semicolons inside the third paragraph are irregular in the source — quotations open without closing, and a closing mark appears where none was opened. The source punctuation has been preserved in body_ar and the English follows it as closely as English punctuation allows. The boundary between the Sheikh's quoted words and the editors' paraphrase is genuinely unclear in places as a result.
'The particularity of the Shinqiti tradition' renders al-khuṣūṣiyyah al-Shinqīṭiyyah, the Mauritanian scholarly tradition in which the Sheikh was trained.
The source spells اللآتي for اللاتي, ولم يتسني for ولم يتسن, and للإستماع with connecting hamza; all preserved in body_ar.
